title: SerreSectionModuleTailFinite
statement: Let k be a field, S=k[x_0,x_1], P=Proj S as in [def-sc-p1-standard], and G a coherent O_P-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Let M be an S-module with additive subgroups M_z, with S_e M_z contained in M_(e+z), and additive isomorphisms phi_z:M_z -> Gamma(P,G tensor O_P(z)) for z>=0 respecting homogeneous multiplication via twistMul of [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf]. There exists N>=0 such that the S-submodule spanned by all M_z with z>=N is finitely generated. No internal direct-sum condition or finiteness of the remaining degrees is required.

source.place: Stacks Project, Lemma 01YS (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01YS), proof of (5); online text read because the local checkout is absent

proof.text: Identify Proj twists and the projective-line twists via the chart isomorphism, proj_shifted_free_is_twist and uniqueness of TwistData. On this noetherian scheme coherence implies quasi-coherence and finite presentation. Obtain a finite twist quotient E -> G with coherent kernel K.

Tensor the kernel sequence with the invertible twist O(d), preserving exactness. Serre vanishing gives N>=0 with H^1(K(d))=0 for all d>=N. The long exact sequence makes the map on global sections of E(d) onto G(d) surjective for these d.

Twist tensor addition and the monomial H^0 calculation identify the graded sections of E with a finite sum of shifts of S. Its tail is a submodule because all polynomial degrees are nonnegative. The Hilbert basis theorem makes S noetherian, so this tail is finite. Through phi inverse the maps of sections define an S-linear map into M; hphi ensures scalar compatibility. Its image is precisely the span of the degrees z>=N, which is finite as a quotient. This also handles E=0 with an empty generating set.
